subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should OpenClaw keep cron failure visibility entirely in the Gateway process, or add a restart-aware/out-of-process stuck-run signal for macOS launchd cron jobs under Gateway memory pressure?
rationale: Source inspection shows current restart accounting and failureAlert delivery remain Gateway-local; deciding whether to add an external watchdog or visible recovery surface is a product and ownership choice, not a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Require soak proof first
options.body: Keep the issue open and require a current-main macOS launchd soak before choosing any new failure-reporting architecture.

options.title: Add restart-aware failure visibility
options.body: Persist started/success lifecycle state and surface missing-success failures after restart without adding a separate watchdog process.

options.title: Add external watchdog alerting
options.body: Introduce an out-of-process launchd-aware watchdog or notifier so cron failure alerts can survive a wedged Gateway event loop.

recommendation.title: Require soak proof first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require a current-main macOS launchd soak before choosing any new failure-reporting architecture.

likelyOwner.reason: The open product choice centers on cron interrupted-run accounting and failure visibility, where recent history points most directly to Yuval Dinodia's commits.
